translations.title: 一周跑步怎么安排：轻松跑、质量课和长距离
translations.summary: 一周训练的价值来自可持续的重复，而不是每天都很硬。先用轻松跑积累时间，再安排少量质量课和一次长距离，并留出真正的恢复日。
translations.body:
## 先确定一周能重复几次

一周计划的第一步不是找一个完美模板，而是确认哪几天真的能跑。NHS 的 Couch to 5K 用每周三次跑、之间安排休息日开始，说明频率本身就是训练结构的一部分。对多数业余跑者，三到四次跑步通常比“这一周每天补课、下一周完全停掉”更容易持续；具体次数仍取决于基础、目标和恢复。

## 轻松跑占大头

轻松跑的目的不是“凑里程”，而是用较低负担积累有氧刺激和跑量。谈话测试仍然适用：能用完整句子交谈，结束时还有余力。若一周只有三次跑步，通常可以让其中两次是轻松跑，另一次安排质量课或长距离；不要把所有跑步都变成比赛配速。

## 质量课只占一小部分

节奏跑、间歇或坡跑属于质量课。它们给身体更强刺激，也带来更高恢复成本。新手不必急着加入；已有基础的人也应把质量课放在精神、睡眠和天气都相对稳定的一天，并避免连续两天高质量。CDC 的成人活动建议强调有氧和每周两次力量练习，后者可以与跑步分开安排。

## 长距离的位置

长距离是练习持续运动、补给和路线判断的场合，不是每周都必须拉到极限。它的长度应相对于当前基础和目标，而不是照搬他人的公里数。长距离后安排轻松日或休息日；如果第二天仍明显疲劳，下一次长距离不应继续加码。

## 留出真正的恢复日

恢复日可以完全休息，也可以是很轻的步行或慢跑；判断标准是结束后不增加疲劳。睡眠、工作和生活压力会改变同一计划的负担，因此每周回看一次：哪次训练后最难恢复？哪一天总被跳过？把不可持续的环节缩小，而不是用意志力硬撑。

## 适用边界

本页不给个体化训练计划，也不保证某个频率适合你的伤病、健康或比赛目标。疼痛、持续疲劳、睡眠恶化或既往伤病，应降低负荷并寻求合格教练或医疗人员评估。

## 来源与适用范围

活动频率和渐进结构参考 NHS Couch to 5K；成人活动量与力量练习参考 CDC；目标与每周记录参考 ODPHP 活动计划工具。它们是一般公共卫生建议，不是个体化处方。

translations.title: A weekly running week: easy runs, quality and the long run
translations.summary: A useful training week comes from repeatable work, not daily hardness. Build time with easy running, add a small amount of quality and one long run, and keep a real recovery day.
translations.body:
## Start with the number of runs you can repeat

The first question is not which perfect template to copy, but which days you can actually run. NHS Couch to 5K begins with three runs a week and rest days between them, which makes frequency part of the training structure. For most amateur runners, three or four runs a week is easier to sustain than “make up every missed day this week, then stop next week”. The right number still depends on your base, goal and recovery.

## Easy running takes most of the week

Easy running is not filler mileage. It accumulates aerobic stimulus and running volume at a manageable cost. The talk test still applies: full sentences are possible and you finish with something left. If you run three times a week, two easy runs plus one quality session or long run is a common shape; do not turn every run into race pace.

## Quality is a small slice

Tempo runs, intervals and hill sessions are quality work. They provide a stronger stimulus and cost more recovery. Beginners do not need to rush into them; experienced runners should place quality on a day when sleep, mood and weather are reasonably stable and avoid stacking hard days. CDC guidance also includes two days of muscle-strengthening activity a week, which can be arranged separately from running.

## Where the long run fits

The long run is a place to practise sustained movement, fuelling and route judgement, not a weekly maximum test. Its length should relate to your current base and goal, not someone else's kilometre count. Follow it with an easy day or rest; if you are still clearly fatigued the next day, do not add more next time.

## Keep a real recovery day

A recovery day can be complete rest or very light walking or jogging; the test is that it does not leave you more tired. Sleep, work and life stress change the cost of the same plan, so review once a week: which session was hardest to recover from? Which day is always skipped? Shrink the unsustainable part instead of forcing it with willpower.

## Scope and limits

This page does not give an individual training plan or promise that a frequency suits your injury history, health or race goal. Pain, persistent fatigue, worsening sleep or a previous injury should prompt a lower load and assessment by a qualified coach or clinician.

## Sources and scope

Frequency and progression follow NHS Couch to 5K; adult activity and strength guidance follow the CDC; goal setting and weekly tracking follow the ODPHP planner. These are general public-health suggestions, not an individual prescription.

sources.title: Biomechanics and Physiology of Uphill and Downhill Running
claims: Uphill running has a higher step frequency, shorter swing and aerial phase, and greater duty factor than level running.
Downhill running has longer aerial time, lower step frequency and more rear-foot striking than level running.
Downhill running emphasises eccentric work and energy dissipation; uphill running requires greater muscular work, particularly at the hip.

translations.title: 上坡与下坡：同一座山，两种跑法
translations.summary: 上坡靠持续做功，下坡靠离心控制。把平路配速搬到坡上，通常只会让上坡过早疲劳、下坡失去控制。
translations.body:
## 坡度改变了动作

上坡时，身体需要把更多质量抬升到更高位置，髋部伸肌和小腿承受的做功增加。为了在较短的支撑时间里完成推进，跑者通常会缩短步幅、提高步频，摆腿幅度和腾空时间减少。下坡则相反：重力帮忙，腾空时间变长，步频往往降低，脚更容易以足跟或全脚掌先落地，肌肉需要用离心收缩吸收冲击。

这意味着“上坡跑慢一点、下坡跑快一点”只对了一半。上坡慢是因为同样的配速需要更高代价；下坡快并不等于可以完全放松，因为冲击和股四头肌负荷也在增加。

## 上坡：用努力而不是配速

上坡最实用的控制指标是呼吸和主观用力，而不是手表上的配速。能保持稳定节奏、呼吸逐渐加深但不混乱，通常比死守平路配速更可持续。坡很陡、路面技术性强或海拔较高时，走路并不丢人；越野比赛里，主动快步走往往比勉强跑更省总时间。

步幅缩短、步频自然提高，身体略微前倾但不要弯腰；手臂摆动帮助节奏，不要跨大步去“够”坡顶。上坡练习可以从 20 到 60 秒的短坡开始，慢跑下来恢复，再做几组；总次数以动作不变形为限。

上坡不是力量房的替代品。它提供的是特定角度的负荷和技术练习，不能代替系统的力量训练、恢复和渐进负荷。

## 下坡：控制比速度重要

下坡时，重力会把你往前拉，但肌肉仍在工作，尤其是股四头肌要吸收落地冲击。步幅突然拉大、脚落在身体前方很远，会让刹车和冲击集中到膝盖和小腿。更可控的做法是保持脚步轻、步幅不要完全放开，落地位置靠近身体下方，视线看远一点，提前选择落脚点。

技术性下坡需要练习。先在短而缓的坡上适应，再逐渐增加长度和不平整度；不要在疲劳末段第一次尝试快速下坡。比赛前查看路线剖面和技术路段说明，把最陡的下坡写进配速和补给计划，而不是等到了坡顶才决定。

## 坡度与天气

湿滑、碎石、树根和积雪会改变抓地与制动，同一坡度在干燥和潮湿条件下完全不是一回事。下坡遇到技术路段时，减速、缩短步幅、必要时侧身或扶稳，比维持速度更安全。高海拔会降低可用氧，呼吸和心率反应更明显，不能用海平面的努力感直接套用。

上坡时如果出现胸痛、眩晕、异常心悸或严重气短，应立即停止并寻求帮助。下坡摔倒后如果出现持续疼痛、肿胀、无法负重或头部撞击，应按急性损伤处理，不要靠继续跑“验证”。

## 适用边界

本页提供一般上下坡技术原则，不替代教练的个体化技术评估、越野导航培训或医疗建议。技术路段、天气和海拔条件变化很大，实际路线应以赛事方和当地管理部门的最新信息为准。

## 来源与适用范围

上坡的步频、支撑时间和髋部做功，以及下坡的腾空时间、步频和离心负荷，参考 Sports Medicine 关于上下坡跑步生物力学与生理学的综述。该综述描述的是群体和实验条件下的规律，不等于每个人的固定技术模板。核验日期为 2026-10-28。

translations.title: Uphill and downhill: one hill, two ways to run it
translations.summary: Uphill running is sustained work; downhill running is eccentric control. Copying flat-road pace onto a gradient usually leaves you tired on the climb and out of control on the descent.
translations.body:
## Gradient changes the movement

Uphill, the body has to lift more mass against gravity, and the hip extensors and lower leg do more work. To produce propulsion in a shorter stance time, runners usually shorten the stride, increase step frequency and reduce swing and flight time. Downhill is different: gravity helps, flight time lengthens, cadence often falls, the foot is more likely to land heel-first or flat, and muscles absorb impact through eccentric work.

So “slower uphill, faster downhill” is only half true. Uphill is slower because the same pace costs more. Downhill is not free speed, because impact and quadriceps load also rise.

## Uphill: effort, not pace

Breathing and perceived effort are more useful than the pace on your watch. A steady rhythm with deeper but controlled breathing is usually more sustainable than defending a flat-road pace. On a steep, technical or high-altitude climb, walking is not a failure; in trail races, purposeful power-hiking often costs less overall than forcing a run.

Shorten the stride, let cadence rise naturally, lean slightly from the ankles rather than folding at the waist, and let the arms support the rhythm. Do not lunge for the top. Start hill sessions with 20–60 second repeats and an easy jog down; stop when form changes.

Hill running is not a replacement for strength training. It provides load and skill practice at a specific angle, not a substitute for progressive strength work, recovery and gradual load management.

## Downhill: control before speed

Gravity pulls you forward, but the muscles still work, especially the quadriceps that absorb landing forces. A suddenly longer stride with the foot far in front concentrates braking and impact in the knee and lower leg. A more controlled descent keeps the steps light, the stride from opening completely, the landing closer under the body, the eyes further ahead and the next foothold chosen early.

Technical descending is a skill. Start on short, gentle slopes and gradually add length and uneven ground. Do not try your first fast descent at the end of a fatigued session. Check the course profile and technical notes before a race, and put the steep descents into the pace and fuelling plan rather than deciding at the top.

## Gradient, weather and altitude

Wet rock, loose gravel, roots and snow change grip and braking; the same gradient is a different problem in dry and wet conditions. On a technical descent, slow down, shorten the stride, turn sideways or use a handhold when needed. Altitude reduces available oxygen, so breathing and heart-rate responses can be much higher than at sea level; do not apply a sea-level effort by feel.

Stop and seek help for chest pain, dizziness, unusual palpitations or severe breathlessness on a climb. After a fall, persistent pain, swelling, inability to bear weight or a head impact should be treated as an acute injury, not tested by running on.

## Scope and limits

This page offers general uphill and downhill principles, not individual coaching, trail-navigation training or medical advice. Technical terrain, weather and altitude vary widely; the organiser and local land manager’s latest information govern the actual route.

## Sources and scope

Uphill step frequency, stance time and hip work, and downhill flight time, cadence and eccentric load, follow a Sports Medicine review of uphill and downhill running biomechanics and physiology. The review describes group and laboratory patterns, not a fixed technical template for every runner. Checked 2026-10-28.

sources.title: Hike Smart
claims: Leave a trip plan with a trusted person including route, contacts, arrival and return times, and companions.
Mobile coverage may be absent; consider a locator beacon and conserve battery.
Check the weather, prepare for lightning and flash flooding, and keep a Plan B.

sources.title: Ten Essentials
claims: The NPS minimum kit includes navigation, sun protection, clothing, illumination, first aid, fire, repair kit, food, water and water-treatment supplies, and shelter.
Navigation means a map, compass and GPS; a physical map should back up electronic tools.
A headlamp with spare batteries is recommended, and someone should know the route and expected return time.

translations.title: 手表心率和 GPS 能说明什么，不能说明什么
translations.summary: 手表可以提供趋势和参考，但 GPS 会漂移、光学心率有延迟，读数也不是医疗诊断。用趋势和主观感受交叉判断，别让数字替代路线与身体信号。
translations.body:
## GPS 是估计，不是认证测量

手表 GPS 在树荫、高楼、山谷、隧道和转弯处可能漂移或丢点；它记录的是设备估计的轨迹，不是赛事丈量。用它比较相同路线的趋势、查看大致配速和位置可以，但不要把它当成精确距离或官方赛道几何。国家公园管理局也提醒 GPS 可能不可靠，应携带替代导航。

## 光学心率有延迟

腕部光学心率通过皮肤血流估计心率，受佩戴松紧、寒冷、肤色、纹身、手臂动作和出汗影响；间歇跑、快速变速或力量训练时可能滞后。胸带通常更稳定，但也可能受干扰。单次异常读数不足以诊断健康问题；看多日趋势和主观用力感。

## 配速和距离会被平滑

手表显示的即时配速常被平滑，短距离冲刺、间歇或 GPS 漂移时可能忽快忽慢；平均配速也会因暂停、自动计圈和隧道丢点而偏差。训练时用分段、路线和主观用力交叉判断，不要为了追一个数字而改变动作或忽略疼痛。

## 电量、导航与安全

长距离或越野时，手表电量、离线地图和备用电源是安全装备的一部分。国家公园管理局建议携带地图/指南针和头灯，手机或手表不能作为唯一导航；出发前告诉别人路线和返回时间。设备数据不能替代对天气、封路和身体信号的判断。

## 适用边界

本页不评价具体品牌或型号，不把腕表心率当作医疗诊断，也不保证 GPS 精度。胸痛、晕厥、异常心悸或持续不适时应停止运动并寻求医疗帮助，而不是继续查看手表。

## 来源与适用范围

GPS 可靠性和替代导航建议参考美国国家公园管理局的 Hike Smart 与十项必备；设备精度和光学心率限制为一般技术说明，具体型号表现需独立测试。

translations.title: What watch heart rate and GPS can and cannot tell you
translations.summary: A watch offers trends and context, but GPS drifts, optical heart rate lags and readings are not a medical diagnosis. Cross-check trends with perceived effort and do not let numbers replace route and body signals.
translations.body:
## GPS is an estimate, not a certified measurement

Watch GPS can drift or lose points under trees, near tall buildings, in valleys, tunnels and turns. It records the device's estimate, not a race-certified course. Use it for trends on the same route and for approximate pace and location, not as precise distance or official geometry. The National Park Service also warns that GPS can be unreliable and recommends alternative navigation.

## Optical heart rate has a delay

Wrist optical heart rate estimates from skin blood flow and can be affected by strap fit, cold, skin tone, tattoos, arm movement and sweat. It may lag during intervals, fast changes or strength work. A chest strap is often more stable but can also be disturbed. A single odd reading cannot diagnose a health problem; look at multi-day trends and perceived effort.

## Pace and distance are smoothed

Instant pace is often smoothed, and short reps, GPS drift or pauses can make it swing; average pace can also be affected by auto-laps and lost points. Cross-check with splits, route and perceived effort, and do not change your movement or ignore pain to chase a number.

## Battery, navigation and safety

For long runs and trails, battery, offline maps and a backup power source are part of safety kit. The National Park Service recommends a map/compass and headlamp; a phone or watch should not be the only navigation. Tell someone your route and return time. Device data cannot replace judgement about weather, closures and body signals.

## Scope and limits

This page does not rank brands or models, treat wrist heart rate as a medical diagnosis or guarantee GPS accuracy. Stop and seek medical help for chest pain, fainting, unusual palpitations or persistent symptoms rather than checking the watch again.

## Sources and scope

GPS reliability and alternative navigation follow the U.S. National Park Service Hike Smart and Ten Essentials pages; device accuracy and optical-heart-rate limits are general technical notes, not model-specific test results.

sources.title: Overtraining syndrome: a practical guide
claims: Overtraining syndrome is described as a maladapted response to excessive exercise without adequate rest, involving neurological, endocrine and immune systems and mood changes.
Persistent fatigue and a decline or plateau in performance should prompt consideration of overtraining syndrome and exclusion of underlying illness.
There is no single diagnostic marker; assessment is clinical and requires identifying contributing training, recovery and health factors.
Management includes rest and correction of the factors that led to the imbalance between training and recovery.

sources.title: Insomnia
claims: Everyone needs different amounts of sleep.
On average, adults need 7 to 9 hours of sleep.
Insomnia means regularly having problems sleeping and usually improves by changing sleeping habits.
Persistent sleep problems can affect daily life and may need medical advice.

translations.title: 手表数据与恢复：看趋势，不要看一次分数
translations.summary: 心率、HRV、睡眠和“恢复分数”能记录变化，但不能诊断疲劳或伤病。单次异常很常见，连续趋势和主观感受更值得一起看。
translations.body:
## 手表能记录什么

跑步手表和手环可以记录配速、心率、步频、海拔、睡眠时长和心率变异性（HRV）等信号，有些还会给出“恢复”“准备度”或“训练负荷”分数。这些数字适合用来观察趋势和安排训练，不适合单独用来判断身体是否健康。

光学心率在低温、手腕松动、肤色较深、手臂摆动或汗液干扰时可能失真；GPS 在城市峡谷、树林和隧道中会漂移；睡眠分期与实验室多导睡眠图并不等同。设备算法和基准值各不相同，两个品牌的分数字不能直接比较。

## 单次异常不是结论

HRV 会受睡眠、酒精、咖啡因、感染、压力和训练影响，一天偏低并不等于过度训练。静息心率偶尔升高也可能是炎热、脱水、晚睡或情绪紧张。把单次读数当成“身体评分”，容易在正常波动里做出过度反应。

更有用的做法是建立自己的基线：连续记录数周，观察同一时间、同一条件下的趋势。如果 HRV 连续多天下降、静息心率持续升高，同时伴随睡眠变差、疲劳、动作沉重或训练表现下降，才值得进一步调整负荷。即使如此，也不能只凭手表诊断过度训练。

## 恢复要看整体

过度训练的识别没有单一生物标志物，通常需要结合训练史、表现下降、疲劳、睡眠和情绪，并排除贫血、甲状腺、感染、抑郁等其他原因。手表分数不能替代这种评估。

睡眠是最值得关注的指标之一，但重点不是追求某个“睡眠分数”，而是规律作息、睡够、白天是否清醒。连续失眠、打鼾伴憋醒、白天严重嗜睡或疲劳持续数周，应寻求医疗评估。

## 怎样把数据用起来

每周回看一次趋势，不要每小时刷新。把训练日志、主观疲劳、疼痛、睡眠和比赛安排放在一起；如果数据与感受冲突，先相信身体感受，再找原因。比赛前不要因为一个“恢复分数”临时改变已经验证过的计划，也不要用数据为带痛训练找理由。

分享数据时注意隐私。路线、心率和睡眠属于个人信息；公开截图前删除位置、姓名和设备标识。没有必要时，不要把完整训练历史交给不熟悉的第三方应用。

## 适用边界

本页不提供个体化训练负荷、HRV 解读或医疗诊断。心律不齐、胸痛、晕厥、持续失眠、严重疲劳或已知心血管疾病的人，应咨询医生；设备报警不能替代急救。

## 来源与适用范围

过度训练相关概念和“没有单一诊断指标、需要排除其他原因”的边界，参考 Current Sports Medicine Reports 的实用综述；持续失眠的就医提示参考 NHS 的失眠页面。消费级设备数据属于趋势参考，不是临床诊断。核验日期为 2026-10-28。

translations.title: Watch data and recovery: read trends, not one score
translations.summary: Heart rate, HRV, sleep and readiness scores can track change, but they cannot diagnose fatigue or injury. A single abnormal reading is common; trends plus how you feel are more useful.
translations.body:
## What a watch can record

Running watches and bands record pace, heart rate, cadence, elevation, sleep duration and heart-rate variability (HRV); some also produce “recovery”, “readiness” or “training load” scores. These numbers are useful for spotting trends and planning training, not for deciding on their own whether the body is healthy.

Optical heart rate can be distorted by cold, a loose strap, darker skin, arm movement or sweat. GPS drifts in urban canyons, forests and tunnels. Sleep staging is not the same as laboratory polysomnography. Algorithms and baselines differ between brands, so two readiness scores are not directly comparable.

## One abnormal reading is not a conclusion

HRV is affected by sleep, alcohol, caffeine, infection, stress and training; one low day does not mean overtraining. Resting heart rate can rise with heat, dehydration, a late night or nerves. Treating a single reading as a body score encourages overreaction to normal variation.

A better approach is to build your own baseline over several weeks, measured at the same time under similar conditions. A sustained fall in HRV, a sustained rise in resting heart rate, worse sleep, fatigue, heavy legs or declining performance may justify adjusting load. Even then, a watch cannot diagnose overtraining.

## Recovery is more than a number

There is no single biomarker for overtraining. Assessment combines training history, performance decline, fatigue, sleep and mood, and excludes other causes such as anaemia, thyroid disease, infection or depression. A device score cannot replace that assessment.

Sleep deserves attention, but the goal is not a perfect sleep score; it is regular, sufficient sleep and feeling awake during the day. Persistent insomnia, snoring with gasping, severe daytime sleepiness or weeks of fatigue warrant medical assessment.

## Using the data well

Review trends once a week rather than refreshing all day. Put training logs, perceived fatigue, pain, sleep and races together. When data and felt experience disagree, start with the body and then look for an explanation. Do not change a tested race plan because of one readiness score, and do not use data to justify running through pain.

Mind privacy when sharing. Routes, heart rate and sleep are personal data; remove location, names and device identifiers from screenshots. Do not hand a complete training history to an unfamiliar third-party app without a reason.

## Scope and limits

This page does not provide individual training-load advice, HRV interpretation or medical diagnosis. People with arrhythmia, chest pain, fainting, persistent insomnia, severe fatigue or known cardiovascular disease should consult a clinician; a device alert is not a substitute for emergency care.

## Sources and scope

The concepts around overtraining, the absence of a single diagnostic marker and the need to exclude other causes follow a practical review in Current Sports Medicine Reports; advice on persistent insomnia follows the NHS insomnia page. Consumer-device data is a trend aid, not a clinical diagnosis. Checked 2026-10-28.

sources.title: Tips for Maintaining Healthy Weight
claims: Healthy pregnant or postpartum women need at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week.
Weight is influenced by factors including sleep, age, genes and medications.
People who are physically active can still gain weight if they take in more calories than they use.
A health care provider is the best person to ask whether illnesses or medications are contributing to weight gain or making weight loss difficult.

sources.title: IOC consensus statement on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs)
sources.license: IOC copyright; citation and summary only
claims: REDs describes a syndrome of health and performance effects associated with low energy availability.
The 2023 IOC consensus updated the earlier female athlete triad framework and applies to both male and female athletes.

translations.title: 体重与跑步：别把轻当成快的代名词
translations.summary: 体重会影响跑步的代谢成本，但快速减重、长期能量不足和比赛目标叠加，可能损害健康与表现。先保证能量可用性，再谈体重。
translations.body:
## 体重不是唯一的性能变量

跑步时要把身体质量反复抬升和减速，体重会影响单位距离的能量消耗。但成绩还取决于训练、耐力、配速、跑步经济性、赛道、天气和恢复。把体重当成唯一变量，容易忽略训练质量和健康状态，也可能把正常的体重波动误当成失败。

CDC 的健康体重建议强调均衡饮食、规律活动和可持续的生活方式，而不是短期极端节食。对跑者来说，足够的碳水和蛋白质是训练和恢复的基础；在能量摄入不足时增加训练，通常只会让疲劳和伤病风险上升。

## 低能量可用性的风险

长期能量可用性不足与 RED-S 相关，可能影响内分泌、骨骼、代谢、心理和运动表现。快速减重、长期低体重、月经改变、反复应力性骨折、持续疲劳、怕冷、睡眠变差或对食物失去控制感，都是需要认真对待的信号。

体重下降不一定意味着表现提升。短期体重下降可能伴随糖原和水分的丢失，长期能量不足则可能降低恢复能力、骨密度和免疫功能，最终让训练无法持续。

## 比赛目标与体重

如果比赛目标需要调整体重，应该在不影响训练和健康的前提下缓慢进行，并由医生或注册营养师评估。不要把比赛日期和减重截止日绑在一起；赛前几周同时增加训练、减少进食和承受比赛压力，是风险最高的组合之一。

训练日需要足够的碳水支持质量课和长距离，恢复日也不需要刻意挨饿。蛋白质分配、蔬菜水果和总能量比“某种神奇食物”更重要。补剂不能替代正常饮食，也不能保证减重或提速。

## 身体形象与求助

对体重、食物和训练失去控制感，反复称重、隐藏进食、因一顿饭感到强烈内疚，或体重已经明显影响健康和社交，应寻求进食障碍或心理健康专业评估。越早处理越容易恢复；不要等到受伤或闭经才重视。

## 适用边界

本页不提供减重计划、热量目标或体脂标准，也不诊断进食障碍、RED-S 或代谢疾病。孕期、哺乳期、青少年、慢性病、糖尿病或进食障碍史的人，应与医生或注册营养师讨论体重和训练目标。

## 来源与适用范围

健康体重和均衡饮食的一般原则参考 CDC 的健康体重建议；低能量可用性与 RED-S 的多系统风险参考国际奥委会的 RED-S 共识页面。体重与表现的关系受多因素影响，本文不提供个体化减重方案。核验日期为 2026-10-28。

translations.title: Weight and running: lighter is not automatically faster
translations.summary: Body weight affects the metabolic cost of running, but rapid weight loss, chronic low energy and race goals can harm health and performance. Protect energy availability before chasing a weight.
translations.body:
## Weight is not the only performance variable

Running repeatedly lifts and decelerates body mass, so weight affects energy cost per kilometre. Performance also depends on training, endurance, pacing, running economy, course, weather and recovery. Treating weight as the only variable ignores training quality and health, and can turn normal fluctuation into a false failure.

CDC healthy-weight guidance emphasises balanced eating, regular activity and a sustainable lifestyle rather than short-term extreme dieting. For runners, enough carbohydrate and protein supports training and recovery; adding training while under-fuelling usually increases fatigue and injury risk.

## Risks of low energy availability

Chronic low energy availability is linked to RED-S and can affect endocrine, bone, metabolic, psychological and performance systems. Rapid weight loss, long-term low body weight, menstrual changes, recurrent stress fractures, persistent fatigue, feeling cold, poor sleep or loss of control around food are signals to take seriously.

Weight loss does not automatically mean better performance. Short-term loss may include glycogen and water; long-term under-fuelling can reduce recovery, bone density and immune function, eventually making training unsustainable.

## Race goals and weight

If a race goal involves changing weight, do it slowly and only when it does not compromise training or health, with a doctor or registered dietitian. Do not tie the race date to a weight-loss deadline; combining more training, less food and race pressure in the final weeks is one of the riskiest combinations.

Training days need enough carbohydrate for quality sessions and long runs; recovery days do not require deliberate hunger. Protein distribution, vegetables and total energy matter more than a “magic” food. Supplements do not replace normal eating or guarantee weight loss or speed.

## Body image and help

Seek eating-disorder or mental-health assessment for loss of control around food, weight or training; repeated weighing, secret eating, intense guilt after a meal, or weight change that affects health and social life. Earlier support is easier; do not wait for injury or missed periods.

## Scope and limits

This page does not provide a weight-loss plan, calorie target or body-fat standard, or diagnose eating disorders, RED-S or metabolic disease. Pregnancy, breastfeeding, adolescents, chronic disease, diabetes or a history of disordered eating should discuss weight and training goals with a doctor or registered dietitian.

## Sources and scope

General healthy-weight and balanced-eating principles follow CDC healthy-weight guidance; the multi-system risks of low energy availability and RED-S follow the International Olympic Committee RED-S consensus page. Weight and performance are multi-factor, and this page does not provide an individual weight-loss plan. Checked 2026-10-28.

translations.title: 比赛补给规划：按小时估算碳水
translations.summary: 根据预计时长和每份补给碳水，给出 30–60 克/小时的规划范围、总量和份数。它不计算补液量，也不替代训练中的试用。
translations.body:
## 这个工具算什么

输入预计运动时长和每份补给（能量胶、饮料或食物）的碳水克数，工具会用 30–60 克/小时的规划范围估算总碳水、份数和大致分发节奏。少于 60 分钟的运动不自动增加碳水，避免把“补给”变成不必要的任务。

计划是起点，不是比赛日处方。同样时长下，强度、天气、肠胃耐受和训练习惯都会改变实际需要。

## 30–60 克/小时是规划范围

ISSN 的立场声明提到，超过 60 分钟的高强度运动可按约 30–60 克/小时补充碳水，并以 6–8% 的碳水-电解质饮料每 10–15 分钟少量摄入。这个范围适合用来做计划，但不应被理解为“越多越好”或“每个人都必须吃到上限”。

如果产品标签不是 25 克，按实际标签输入。份数向上取整，是为了提醒你准备足够；实际分配仍需在训练中调整。更高摄入量不是本工具的默认建议，尤其不要在没有练习的情况下首次尝试。

## 补水要单独计划

本工具只估算碳水，不估算液体和钠。出汗量受体重、天气、强度、衣物和个人差异影响，固定升数很容易误导。请参考补水文章，结合口渴、尿液颜色、训练前后体重变化和补给点安排液体。

比赛日不要第一次使用新的胶、饮料、盐丸或高浓度配方。先在相似强度和时长的训练中试用，记录胃肠感受和能量变化。

## 怎样使用结果

把总量分配到补给点或携带份数中，设一个简单的提醒节奏，例如每 20–30 分钟少量摄入；不要等到明显饥饿或乏力才开始。长距离或越野比赛要预留“多一份”的余量，并确认补给点之间能否携带足够的水和食物。

如果计划导致腹胀、恶心、频繁停下或能量波动，先降低浓度或份量，再考虑调整产品；持续胃肠问题应寻求运动营养或医疗专业人士建议。

## 适用边界

本工具不提供个体化营养处方、疾病饮食建议、补液量或比赛医疗许可。糖尿病、胃肠疾病、孕期、进食障碍史或用药者，应与医生或注册营养师讨论。

## 来源与适用范围

碳水摄入范围参考 ISSN 的营养时机立场声明；日常与运动补水提示参考 NHS。工具采用保守的 30–60 克/小时规划范围，不覆盖所有运动、气候和个体情况。

translations.title: Race fueling planner: estimate carbohydrate by hour
translations.summary: Use planned duration and carbohydrate per serving to get a 30–60 g/h planning range, total amount and serving count. It does not calculate fluid and does not replace testing in training.
translations.body:
## What this tool calculates

Enter the planned exercise duration and the carbohydrate grams in one serving (gel, drink or food). The tool uses a 30–60 g/h planning range to estimate total carbohydrate, serving count and a rough distribution. Sessions under 60 minutes do not automatically add carbohydrate, so fueling does not become a task with no purpose.

The plan is a starting point, not a race-day prescription. Intensity, weather, gut tolerance and training habits all change what is practical at the same duration.

## The 30–60 g/h range

The ISSN nutrient-timing position stand describes about 30–60 g of carbohydrate per hour for extended high-intensity exercise beyond 60 minutes, taken as a 6–8% carbohydrate-electrolyte solution every 10–15 minutes. That range is useful for planning, not a rule that everyone must reach the top end.

If a product label says something other than 25 g, enter the actual label value. Servings are rounded up so you carry enough; the distribution still needs adjustment in training. Higher intakes are not the tool's default recommendation, especially without practice.

## Fluid is a separate plan

This tool estimates carbohydrate only, not fluid or sodium. Sweat rate varies with body size, weather, intensity, clothing and the individual; a fixed litre target easily misleads. Use the hydration guidance with thirst, urine colour, pre/post-run weight change and aid-station spacing.

Do not try a new gel, drink, salt tablet or concentrated formula for the first time on race day. Test it in training at similar intensity and duration, and record gut comfort and energy.

## Using the result

Split the total across aid stations or carried servings, and set a simple reminder such as a small amount every 20–30 minutes; do not wait for obvious hunger or fatigue. For long or trail races, carry one extra portion and check whether you can carry enough fluid and food between stations.

If the plan causes bloating, nausea, frequent stops or energy swings, reduce concentration or portion size before changing products. Persistent gut problems deserve advice from a sports-nutrition or medical professional.

## Tool limits

This tool does not provide an individual nutrition prescription, therapeutic diet, fluid target or medical clearance. People with diabetes, gastrointestinal disease, pregnancy, a history of disordered eating or medication use should discuss the plan with a clinician or registered dietitian.

## Sources and scope

Carbohydrate ranges follow the ISSN nutrient-timing position stand; everyday and exercise hydration guidance follows the NHS. The tool uses a conservative 30–60 g/h planning range and does not cover every sport, climate or individual.

sources.title: Marathon — World Athletics disciplines
claims: The marathon is a road running event over 42.195 kilometres.
The distance is also expressed as 26 miles and 385 yards.

translations.title: 配速计算器：距离、时间、配速与速度互换
translations.summary: 在距离、时间和配速三项中任选两项，求出第三项，并同时显示每公里配速、每英里配速与平均速度。适用于公路跑的算术换算，不考虑坡度、停顿和风向。
translations.body:
## 这个工具回答什么

配速计算器允许你在三个量中给定两个，求剩下的一个：

- **距离 + 时间**：得到每公里配速、每英里配速和平均速度。
- **距离 + 配速**：得到完成该距离所需的总时间。
- **时间 + 配速**：得到在这段时间内按该配速能跑多远。

页面始终同时给出每公里配速、每英里配速、速度、距离与总时间，方便在公里和英里之间核对。例如，10 公里用 50 分钟完成，平均配速是 5 分 00 秒/公里，速度是 12 公里/小时；反过来，10 公里按 5 分 00 秒/公里跑，需要 50 分钟。

## 公式与单位

内部统一使用米和秒，只在输入和输出边界换算单位。

- 公里转米：距离 × 1000。
- 英里转米：距离 × 1,609.344。
- 距离 + 时间：`每公里配速 = 总秒数 ÷ 距离（公里）`。
- 距离 + 配速：`总秒数 = 配速秒数 × 距离（米） ÷ 配速单位米数`。
- 时间 + 配速：`距离（米） = 总秒数 ÷ 配速秒数 × 配速单位米数`。
- `每英里配速 = 每公里配速 × 1.609344`。
- `速度（公里/小时） = 距离（公里） ÷ (总秒数 ÷ 3600)`。

配速四舍五入到整秒，速度保留两位小数，距离保留三位小数。输入配速时，它表示所选单位下每公里或每英里的时间。计算结果始终是**平均值**。

## 输入与边界

每次必须给出两个有限且大于零的值：距离与时间、距离与配速，或时间与配速。工具不会判断输入是否现实，也不会因为配速过快或过慢而给出训练建议。马拉松距离为 42.195 公里，半程马拉松为 21.0975 公里；如果你输入 42.2 公里，得到的是 42.2 公里的结果，而不是标准马拉松距离。

配速输入使用 `hh:mm:ss` 或 `mm:ss`，例如 `05:00` 表示每公里或每英里 5 分钟。切换单位时，配速的含义也随之切换；不要把每英里配速直接当成每公里配速。

## 怎样解读结果

平均配速适合做赛前目标换算和赛后复盘，但不能描述比赛过程。起跑拥堵、补给站停留、坡度和天气都会让实际分段偏离平均值。若需要逐段计划，使用[分段配速表](/tools/splits/)；若想理解马拉松距离的定义，可阅读知识站的[马拉松为什么是 42.195 公里](https://learn.paobu.org/articles/marathon-distance/)。

配速与速度不是训练强度的同义词。同样的 6 分/公里，在轻松跑和节奏跑中的意义不同；强度判断应结合呼吸、主观用力感和训练目的。

## 验证算例

- 10 公里、3000 秒：300 秒/公里（5:00/公里），482.8032 → 483 秒/英里，12.00 公里/小时。
- 5 英里、2400 秒：480 秒/英里（8:00/英里），298.258 → 298 秒/公里，12.07008 → 12.07 公里/小时。
- 10 公里、300 秒/公里：总时间 3000 秒，速度 12 公里/小时。
- 2400 秒、480 秒/英里：距离 5 英里，即 8.04672 公里，配速 298.258 → 298 秒/公里。

算例由独立算术核对，不依赖页面脚本自身的输出。

## 隐私与数据

所有计算在浏览器本地完成，不上传到应用数据库，也不需要账户。为了刷新后恢复和分享，输入会写入当前网址的查询参数；打开或刷新页面时该网址会随请求发送到静态托管方，也会留在浏览器历史中。文件内容不会写入网址。公共设备上使用后请清除地址栏参数。

## 来源与适用范围

马拉松标准距离依据 World Athletics 的项目说明；英里换算采用国际英里的精确定义。本文与工具核验日期为 2026-10-27。

translations.title: Pace calculator: distance, time, pace and speed
translations.summary: Choose any two of distance, time and pace to solve the third, with pace per kilometre, pace per mile and average speed shown together. A road-running arithmetic tool that does not model hills, stops or wind.
translations.body:
## What this tool answers

The pace calculator works with three quantities and lets you supply any two:

- **Distance + time**: get pace per kilometre, pace per mile and average speed.
- **Distance + pace**: get the total time needed to cover the distance.
- **Time + pace**: get the distance covered at that pace in the given time.

The page always shows pace per kilometre, pace per mile, speed, distance and total time together, so you can check the conversion across units. For example, 10 km in 50 minutes is an average pace of 5:00 per kilometre and a speed of 12 km/h. In reverse, 10 km at 5:00 per kilometre takes 50 minutes.

## Formula and units

The calculation uses metres and seconds internally and converts units only at the input and output boundaries.

- Kilometres to metres: distance × 1000.
- Miles to metres: distance × 1,609.344.
- Distance + time: `pace per kilometre = total seconds ÷ distance in kilometres`.
- Distance + pace: `total seconds = pace seconds × distance in metres ÷ metres per pace unit`.
- Time + pace: `distance in metres = total seconds ÷ pace seconds × metres per pace unit`.
- `pace per mile = pace per kilometre × 1.609344`.
- `speed in km/h = distance in kilometres ÷ (total seconds ÷ 3600)`.

Pace is rounded to the nearest whole second, speed to two decimal places, and distance to three decimal places. A pace input means the time per kilometre or per mile in the selected unit. The result is always an **average**.

## Inputs and limits

Each calculation needs two finite values greater than zero: distance and time, distance and pace, or time and pace. The tool does not judge whether an input is realistic and gives no training advice for fast or slow results. A marathon is 42.195 km and a half marathon is 21.0975 km; if you enter 42.2 km, you get the result for 42.2 km, not the standard marathon distance.

Enter pace as `hh:mm:ss` or `mm:ss`; `05:00` means five minutes per kilometre or per mile. When you change the unit, the meaning of the pace changes with it. Do not treat a per-mile pace as a per-kilometre pace.

## Reading the result

Average pace is useful for pre-race target conversion and post-race review, but it does not describe the race itself. Start corrals, aid-station stops, hills and weather all push actual splits away from the average. For a segment-by-segment plan, use the [split table](/en/tools/splits/). To understand the marathon distance, read [why the marathon is 42.195 km](https://learn.paobu.org/en/articles/marathon-distance/).

Pace and speed are not synonyms for training intensity. The same 6:00 per kilometre means different things in an easy run and a tempo run; judge intensity with breathing, perceived effort and the purpose of the session.

## Verification cases

- 10 km, 3000 seconds: 300 s/km (5:00/km), 482.8032 → 483 s/mi, 12.00 km/h.
- 5 miles, 2400 seconds: 480 s/mi (8:00/mi), 298.258 → 298 s/km, 12.07008 → 12.07 km/h.
- 10 km at 300 s/km: total time 3000 seconds and speed 12 km/h.
- 2400 seconds at 480 s/mi: distance 5 miles, or 8.04672 km, with pace 298.258 → 298 s/km.

These cases were checked by independent arithmetic, not by the page script itself.

## Privacy and data

All calculations happen locally in your browser; inputs are not sent to an application database and no account is required. To restore inputs after a refresh and to support sharing, values are written into the page URL query string. Opening or refreshing that URL sends it to the static host and leaves it in browser history. File contents are never written into the URL. Clear the address-bar parameters after using a shared device.

## Sources and scope

The standard marathon distance follows World Athletics' discipline description; mile conversion uses the exact international mile. This article and tool were checked on 2026-10-27.

A headlamp with spare batteries is recommended, and someone should know the route and expected return time.

translations.title: 赛前清单：按路面、时长和天气生成检查表
translations.summary: 选择公路或越野、预计时长、天气和是否异地参赛，生成可打印的装备、补给、导航和赛后清单。赛事强制装备仍以组委会为准。
translations.body:
## 清单解决什么问题

比赛前最容易漏掉的不是大件，而是号码布固定扣、备用电池、赛后干衣、药物或返程安排。选择比赛类型、预计时长、天气和是否异地参赛，工具会把基础项目和对应条件下的额外项目分节列出。

它是准备提示，不是赛事规则。组委会的强制装备、路线说明、医疗要求和当地法规优先于这份清单。

## 基础、天气与地形

基础部分包括参赛身份、衣物与鞋、补给与水、交通与赛后。越野会额外加入头灯、备用电池、地图/指北针、哨子、急救包、求生毯和撤离计划；超过 6 小时会提醒备用电源、额外食物、足部护理和换装计划。

高温会加入降温、补给点和热病停止信号；寒冷或下雨会加入防风防水层、手套、干燥袋和失温撤离计划。异地参赛会提醒把比赛装备放在随身行李、携带药物并核对当地交通和规则。

## 怎么使用

提前几天生成清单，先处理需要购买、清洗或试用的项目；比赛前一天再核对一次。把“已勾选”当作“已记得”，不是“已测试”。新鞋、新胶、新背包或新药物都不应该在比赛日第一次使用。

打印清单时，浏览器只打印当前页面内容，不会上传选项。清单不保存个人数据；如果你在公共设备上使用，关闭页面即可。

## 适用边界

本清单不替代赛事的强制装备列表、技术会议、医疗建议或路线安全判断。技术性山径、极端天气、夜间赛段或需要绳索的路线，需要专门培训和当地信息。

## 来源与适用范围

越野最低装备框架参考 NPS Ten Essentials；出行计划与手机信号边界参考 NPS Hike Smart；热病停止信号参考 NWS；冬季路线和保暖参考 NPS。具体需求以赛事规则、路线管理和天气预报为准。

translations.title: Race-day checklist: generate by surface, duration and weather
translations.summary: Choose road or trail, expected duration, weather and travel to generate a printable gear, fuel, navigation and finish checklist. The organiser's mandatory kit still takes precedence.
translations.body:
## What the checklist solves

The items most often forgotten before a race are not the big ones: bib fasteners, spare batteries, dry clothes, medication or the return plan. Choose the race type, expected duration, weather and whether you are travelling, and the tool groups baseline items with extra items for those conditions.

It is a preparation prompt, not a race rulebook. The organiser's mandatory kit, route briefing, medical requirements and local regulations take precedence.

## Baseline, weather and terrain

The baseline covers entry and identity, clothing and shoes, fuel and water, and travel and finish. Trail adds a headlamp and spare batteries, map/compass, whistle, first-aid kit, emergency blanket and escape plan. Over six hours adds spare power, extra food, foot care and a drop-bag plan.

Heat adds cooling, aid-station and heat-illness stop signals. Cold or rain adds a wind/water-resistant shell, gloves, a dry bag and a hypothermia exit plan. Travelling adds carry-on race kit, medication, local transport and rule checks.

## How to use it

Generate the list a few days ahead, then handle anything that needs buying, washing or testing. Check again the day before. Treat a tick as “remembered”, not “tested”. New shoes, gels, packs or medication should not make their race debut on the start line.

Printing uses only the current page and does not upload the selections. The checklist does not save personal data; close the page on a shared device.

## Tool limits

This checklist does not replace a race's mandatory kit list, technical briefing, medical advice or route-safety assessment. Technical trails, extreme weather, night sections or roped routes require specific training and local information.

## Sources and scope

The trail minimum-kit framework follows the NPS Ten Essentials; trip planning and phone-coverage limits follow NPS Hike Smart; heat stop signals follow the NWS; winter route and warmth guidance follows the NPS. Actual needs depend on race rules, land-manager guidance and the forecast.

translations.title: 比赛成绩估算：Riegel 公式与 1.06 指数
translations.summary: 用一场已知公路成绩，按 Riegel 模型估算 5 公里至马拉松范围内另一距离的完赛时间与配速。结果只是经验估算，不是成绩保证。
translations.body:
## 这个工具回答什么

输入一场已知公路比赛的**距离**和**完赛时间**，再输入目标距离，工具会用 Riegel 公式估算目标距离的完赛时间，并换算成每公里配速、每英里配速和平均速度。

例如，已知 5 公里跑 20 分钟，估算 10 公里成绩；或已知 10 公里跑 50 分钟，估算半程马拉松成绩。它适合做参赛距离之间的粗略换算，帮助你判断目标时间是否大致处在同一水平，而不是预测比赛当天一定跑出多少。

## 公式与单位

工具采用的公式是：

`目标时间 = 已知时间 × (目标距离 ÷ 已知距离)^1.06`

距离内部统一换算为米，时间使用秒，只在显示时换算成每公里配速、每英里配速与公里/小时。已知距离和目标距离都必须落在 5,000 米至 42,195 米之间；这个范围覆盖 5 公里、10 公里、半程马拉松和马拉松等常见公路距离。

指数 1.06 是产品采用的固定默认值，不是对所有跑者、所有距离都成立的定律。Riegel 公式会为每位跑者拟合一个常数，产品并不根据你的个人数据重新拟合；它只是把 1.06 当作常用的经验简化。

## 适用范围与限制

- 只适用于**公路比赛**，不用于越野、超马或带大量爬升的路线。
- 假设已知成绩与目标比赛之间的训练水平、配速策略和比赛条件大致可比。
- 不提供置信区间，也不给出“达到目标时间的概率”。
- 不考虑天气、气温、海拔、赛道起伏、起跑拥堵或补给策略。
- 不能替代训练计划；不要用估算结果直接安排训练强度或比赛目标。

如果两场比赛相隔很久，或你的训练量、体重、伤病状态发生了明显变化，估算的参考价值会下降。长距离比赛的掉速通常比公式更复杂，尤其在全马后半程。

## 怎样解读结果

先看估算时间，再看对应的平均配速。若目标配速明显快于你目前能稳定完成的训练配速，这更可能说明目标定得激进，而不是你“只差一个公式”。把估算当作起点，再用一场短距离比赛或节奏跑检验，比直接把它当成比赛目标更稳妥。

需要把估算时间转成逐段计划时，使用[分段配速表](/tools/splits/)；需要核对距离、时间和配速的换算，使用[配速计算器](/tools/pace/)。马拉松标准距离的背景可阅读[马拉松为什么是 42.195 公里](https://learn.paobu.org/articles/marathon-distance/)。

## 验证算例

- 已知 5,000 米 1,200 秒，目标 10,000 米：距离比 2，估算 1,200 × 2^1.06 = 2,501.918 秒，显示 2,502 秒；约 250 秒/公里、403 秒/英里、14.39 公里/小时。
- 已知 10,000 米 3,000 秒，目标 21,097.5 米：距离比 2.10975，估算 6,619.209 秒，显示 6,619 秒；约 314 秒/公里、505 秒/英里、11.47 公里/小时。
- 已知 21,097.5 米 5,700 秒，目标 42,195 米：距离比 2，估算 11,884.110 秒，显示 11,884 秒；约 282 秒/公里、453 秒/英里、12.78 公里/小时。

算例由独立算术核对，不依赖页面脚本自身的输出。

## 隐私与数据

所有计算在浏览器本地完成，不上传到应用数据库，也不需要账户。为了刷新后恢复和分享，输入会写入当前网址的查询参数；打开或刷新页面时该网址会随请求发送到静态托管方，也会留在浏览器历史中。文件内容不会写入网址。公共设备上使用后请清除地址栏参数。

## 来源与局限

公式与 1.06 指数的背景参考 Blythe 与 Király 2016 年发表于 PLoS One 的《Prediction and Quantification of Individual Athletic Performance of Runners》，该文说明 Riegel 公式通过为每位跑者拟合常数并将指数固定为 1.06 来做预测。马拉松标准距离参考 World Athletics 的项目说明。本文与工具核验日期为 2026-10-27；模型的适用边界属于已发布的限制说明。

translations.title: Race time prediction: the Riegel formula and its 1.06 exponent
translations.summary: Use one known road race result to estimate the finish time and pace at another distance from 5 km to the marathon under the Riegel model. An empirical estimate, not a promise.
translations.body:
## What this tool answers

Enter the **distance** and **finish time** of a known road race, then enter a target distance. The tool applies the Riegel formula to estimate the target finish time and converts it to pace per kilometre, pace per mile and average speed.

For example, estimate a 10 km time from a 5 km result, or a half marathon from a 10 km result. This is useful for a rough conversion between race distances and for checking whether a target time is broadly in line with current performance. It does not predict what you will definitely run on race day.

## Formula and units

The tool uses:

`target time = known time × (target distance ÷ known distance)^1.06`

Distances are converted to metres internally and time is handled in seconds; conversion to pace per kilometre, pace per mile and km/h happens only for display. Both the known and target distance must be between 5,000 and 42,195 metres, covering common road distances such as 5 km, 10 km, the half marathon and the marathon.

The exponent 1.06 is a fixed product default, not a law that holds for every runner and every distance. The Riegel formula fits a constant to each runner; this tool does not refit anything to your personal data and simply treats 1.06 as a common empirical simplification.

## Scope and limits

- Road races only. Do not use it for trail races, ultramarathons or courses with substantial climbing.
- Assumes the known result and the target race are broadly comparable in training, pacing and conditions.
- No confidence interval and no probability of hitting the target time.
- Weather, heat, altitude, course profile, start congestion and fuelling are not modelled.
- Not a training plan. Do not use the estimate to prescribe training intensity or a race goal on its own.

If the two races are far apart in time, or your training volume, body weight or injury status has changed significantly, the estimate is less useful. Pacing decay over long races is usually more complex than the formula suggests, especially in the second half of a marathon.

## Reading the result

Look at the estimated time first, then the corresponding average pace. If the target pace is much faster than a pace you can currently sustain in training, the goal is more likely too aggressive than the formula being "all that stands between you" and the time. Treat the estimate as a starting point and test it with a shorter race or a tempo effort rather than adopting it as a race goal unexamined.

To turn the estimated time into a segment plan, use the [split table](/en/tools/splits/). To check distance, time and pace conversions, use the [pace calculator](/en/tools/pace/). For background on the marathon distance, read [why the marathon is 42.195 km](https://learn.paobu.org/en/articles/marathon-distance/).

## Verification cases

- Known 5,000 m in 1,200 s, target 10,000 m: distance ratio 2, estimate 1,200 × 2^1.06 = 2,501.918 s, displayed as 2,502 s; about 250 s/km, 403 s/mi and 14.39 km/h.
- Known 10,000 m in 3,000 s, target 21,097.5 m: distance ratio 2.10975, estimate 6,619.209 s, displayed as 6,619 s; about 314 s/km, 505 s/mi and 11.47 km/h.
- Known 21,097.5 m in 5,700 s, target 42,195 m: distance ratio 2, estimate 11,884.110 s, displayed as 11,884 s; about 282 s/km, 453 s/mi and 12.78 km/h.

These values were checked by independent arithmetic, not by the page script itself.

## Privacy and data

All calculations happen locally in your browser; inputs are not sent to an application database and no account is required. To restore inputs after a refresh and to support sharing, values are written into the page URL query string. Opening or refreshing that URL sends it to the static host and leaves it in browser history. File contents are never written into the URL. Clear the address-bar parameters after using a shared device.

## Sources and limitations

The formula and the 1.06 exponent are documented in Blythe and Király, "Prediction and Quantification of Individual Athletic Performance of Runners", PLoS One, 2016, which describes the Riegel formula as fitting a constant to each runner while fixing the exponent at 1.06. The standard marathon distance follows World Athletics. This article and tool were checked on 2026-10-27; the model limits are part of the published scope.

translations.title: 赛道比较：按已发布版本对照距离、高程与技术性
translations.summary: 同时选择 2 至 4 个已发布赛道版本，逐字段对照距离、高程口径、路面与技术性。缺失值显示为未知，不生成安全或难度排名。
translations.body:
## 这个工具做什么

赛道比较把 2 至 4 个**已发布**的赛道版本放在同一张表里，逐字段显示：

- 比赛距离与记录方式。
- 高程爬升（如果已记录）与记录口径。
- 路面类型（如果已记录）。
- 技术性（如果已记录）。

它不做排序，也不把距离更长、爬升更多或技术性字段的某个值解释为“更难”或“更危险”。赛道是否适合你，取决于训练、天气、补给、通行规则和当天状态，不能由一张字段表推导。

## 为什么强调“已发布版本”

赛道数据在发布完成前可能变化，因此未发布的版本不参与比较。工具只读取状态为已发布的固定版本，并显示版本标识；这样你看到的是核验过的记录，而不是编辑中的草稿。

如果当前站点没有足够的已发布版本（少于两个），页面会显示空状态，说明暂无可比较的版本。这不是页面故障，而是内容还没有完成核验并发布。

## 缺失值与口径

缺失的高程、路面或技术性字段显示为**未知**，不会填成 0，也不会因为另一条赛道有值就推断这一条也有。两条赛道的距离可能来自不同的官方说明或测量方式，高程也可能分别来自官方累计爬升、地图估算或轨迹统计；表格会保留各自的口径说明，避免把不同来源的数字当成同一把尺子。

轨迹几何是否公开、是否允许再分发，与能否比较字段是两件事。赛道页面可见不代表轨迹可以转载；需要轨迹时请查看该赛道记录的官方链接与许可说明。

## 验证算例

一个合成验收算例包含两条赛道：第一条距离 42,195 米、爬升 300 米、路面为 road、技术性缺失；第二条距离 21,097.5 米，爬升、路面与技术性都缺失。比较结果应保留两列数值，将第二条的爬升、路面与技术性显示为未知，且不产生任何排名字段。该算例只用于验证字段处理，不代表真实赛事数据。

## 隐私与数据

所有计算在浏览器本地完成，不上传到应用数据库，也不需要账户。为了刷新后恢复和分享，输入会写入当前网址的查询参数；打开或刷新页面时该网址会随请求发送到静态托管方，也会留在浏览器历史中。文件内容不会写入网址。公共设备上使用后请清除地址栏参数。

## 来源与适用范围

马拉松标准距离参考 World Athletics；UTMB 与波士顿马拉松的示例字段来自各自官方页面。工具只展示已记录字段，不认证赛道距离，也不判断赛事安全性。本文与工具核验日期为 2026-10-27。

translations.title: Route comparison: distance, elevation basis and technicality across published versions
translations.summary: Compare two to four published route versions field by field: distance, elevation basis, surface and technicality. Missing values stay unknown, and no safety or difficulty ranking is generated.
translations.body:
## What this tool does

Route comparison places two to four **published** route versions in one table and shows:

- the course distance and how it was recorded;
- elevation gain, when recorded, and its stated basis;
- surface type, when recorded;
- technicality, when recorded.

It does not sort the routes, and it does not interpret a longer distance, more elevation or a particular technicality value as "harder" or "more dangerous". Whether a course suits you depends on training, weather, fuelling, access rules and race-day conditions; a field table cannot derive that.

## Why published versions only

Course data can change before publication is complete, so unpublished versions do not take part. The tool reads only fixed versions whose status is published and shows the version identifier, so you are looking at reviewed records rather than a draft.

If the site does not have enough published versions (fewer than two), the page shows an empty state explaining that nothing is comparable yet. That is a content state, not a page failure.

## Missing values and measurement basis

A missing elevation, surface or technicality field is shown as **unknown**. It is never filled with zero, and a value is not inferred for one route because another route has it. Distance may come from different official descriptions or measurement methods, and elevation may come from official gain, map estimates or track statistics. The table keeps each route's stated basis so numbers from different sources are not treated as one ruler.

Whether track geometry is public or redistributable is separate from whether fields can be compared. A visible route page does not mean its track may be republished; follow the official link and licence note recorded for that route.

## Verification case

A synthetic acceptance case contains two routes. The first has a distance of 42,195 m, 300 m of gain, surface "road" and no technicality. The second has a distance of 21,097.5 m and no elevation, surface or technicality. The comparison must keep both distance values, show the second route's missing fields as unknown and produce no ranking field. This case tests field handling only and does not represent a real race.

## Privacy and data

All calculations happen locally in your browser; inputs are not sent to an application database and no account is required. To restore inputs after a refresh and to support sharing, values are written into the page URL query string. Opening or refreshing that URL sends it to the static host and leaves it in browser history. File contents are never written into the URL. Clear the address-bar parameters after using a shared device.

## Sources and scope

The standard marathon distance follows World Athletics; example fields for UTMB and the Boston Marathon come from their official pages. The tool displays recorded fields only, does not certify course distance and does not judge race safety. This article and tool were checked on 2026-10-27.

translations.title: 路线高程分析：本地读取 GPX 的高程剖面
translations.summary: 读取 GPX 或 GeoJSON，计算距离、累计爬升/下降、海拔范围和最大坡度，并显示降采样后的高程剖面。高程缺失时保持未知，不按零处理。
translations.body:
## 工具做什么

选择本地 GPX 或 GeoJSON 文件，工具会在当前浏览器内读取轨迹，计算总距离、累计爬升、累计下降、最低/最高海拔和相邻点之间的最大绝对坡度，并绘制高程剖面。文件不会上传，也不需要账户。

它适合在出发前了解路线起伏，或核对一次活动记录的高程结构。它不是赛事认证、路线安全评估或导航工具。

## 距离、爬升和坡度的口径

距离按每条线段内相邻点的 WGS84 大圆距离累加；不同线段分别计算，不把线段端点人为连接。累计爬升是所有正向高差之和，累计下降是所有负向高差绝对值之和。

坡度使用相邻点的 `Δ海拔 / 水平距离 × 100%`；为避免过近采样点放大噪声，只对水平距离至少 5 米的点对计算。最大坡度因此是点对估计，不是公路设计坡度，也不能代表整段路线的平均难度。

## 高程缺失与 GPS 噪声

如果文件完全没有高程，或只有部分点有高程，工具会把累计爬升、下降和剖面显示为未知，而不是把缺失值当作 0；否则会低估爬升。GPS 高程本身会有漂移，不同设备、气压计和修正算法可能给出不同的累计爬升。

若需要比较两条路线，尽量使用同一来源和同一高程口径；不要把设备自动修正前后的数字直接混用。

## 怎样使用

先看总距离和爬升量级，再看剖面中的陡升、陡降和长坡位置；结合补给点、路面和天气阅读。对于比赛路线，仍需以组委会公布的路线、强制装备和技术说明为准，不能只凭一个 GPX 文件判断安全性。

文件在本地解析；关闭页面后结果不会保存。若文件过大或格式异常，工具会给出错误提示，不会生成半成品结果。

## 适用边界

本工具不验证赛道是否为官方版本、是否获得通行许可、是否适合比赛，也不评估落石、交通、天气或技术难度。技术性山径、冰川或需要绳索的路线，需要专门培训和当地信息。

## 来源与适用范围

GPX 与 GeoJSON 的格式边界参考公开规范；上下坡的力学差异参考运动生物力学综述。高程数值来自文件本身，工具不对设备精度或路线安全作保证。

translations.title: Route elevation profile: read a GPX file locally
translations.summary: Read GPX or GeoJSON, calculate distance, gain, loss, elevation range and maximum grade, and show a downsampled profile. Missing elevation stays unknown rather than becoming zero.
translations.body:
## What this tool does

Choose a local GPX or GeoJSON file. The tool reads the track in this browser, calculates total distance, cumulative gain and loss, minimum and maximum elevation, the largest absolute point-to-point grade, and draws an elevation profile. The file is not uploaded and no account is required.

It is useful for understanding the shape of a route before heading out or reviewing the elevation structure of a recorded activity. It is not race certification, a safety assessment or a navigation tool.

## How distance, gain and grade are defined

Distance is the sum of WGS84 great-circle distances between consecutive points within each segment. Segments are measured independently and their endpoints are not joined. Gain is the sum of all positive elevation differences; loss is the sum of the absolute negative differences.

Grade is `Δelevation / horizontal distance × 100%`. To avoid amplifying noise from points that are very close together, grade is calculated only for pairs at least 5 metres apart. The maximum grade is therefore a point-pair estimate, not a road-design grade or a whole-climb average.

## Missing elevation and GPS noise

If the file has no elevation, or only some points have it, the tool shows gain, loss and profile as unknown instead of treating missing values as zero; otherwise it would undercount climbing. GPS elevation also drifts, and different devices, barometers and correction algorithms can produce different totals.

When comparing two routes, prefer the same source and the same elevation method. Do not mix corrected and uncorrected numbers without saying so.

## Using the result

Start with the distance and climb magnitude, then look for steep climbs, descents and long gradients in the profile. Read them alongside aid stations, surface and weather. For a race, the organiser's route, mandatory kit and technical notes remain authoritative; a GPX file alone cannot establish safety.

Parsing happens locally. Results are not saved after the page closes. Oversized or malformed files return an error rather than a partial result.

## Tool limits

This tool does not verify that a track is the official course, that access is permitted or that the route is suitable for a race. It does not assess rockfall, traffic, weather or technical difficulty. Technical trails, glaciers or roped routes require specific training and local information.

## Sources and scope

GPX and GeoJSON format boundaries follow the public specifications; uphill and downhill mechanics follow a sports-biomechanics review. Elevation values come from the file; the tool does not guarantee device accuracy or route safety.

translations.title: 跑走交替计划：按循环数或总时长排版
translations.summary: 用于跑走结合训练：输入每轮跑步与步行时长，按循环数或总时长列出逐段安排，并明确最后一段是否被截断。只做时间换算，不推算距离、配速或训练效果。
translations.body:
## 这个工具回答什么

跑走交替计划把“跑多久、走多久、做几轮”变成一张可以照着执行的逐段表。它有两种输入方式：

- **循环数模式**：给定每轮跑步时长、步行时长和循环数，列出每一轮的跑步段与步行段。最后一轮的步行也包含在计划里，不会被省略。
- **总时长模式**：给定每轮跑步与步行时长，以及一个总时长，工具从第一轮开始依次排列，直到用完总时长。如果总时长落在某一段中间，最后一段会被截断并标记为“不完整”。

工具输出请求时长、计划总时长、完整轮数、逐段明细、跑步总时长、步行总时长，以及末段是否被截断。它不会根据时长反推你跑了多远，也不会估计消耗的热量。

## 两种排法的细节

**循环数模式**：每轮固定为“跑步 + 步行”。例如跑步 2 分钟、步行 1 分钟、共 3 轮，计划总时长为 3 × (2 + 1) = 9 分钟，其中跑步 6 分钟、步行 3 分钟，共 6 段。若步行时长设为 0，则不会生成空的步行段，计划只剩跑步段。

**总时长模式**：工具不断重复跑步与步行，直到达到总时长。以跑步 2 分钟、步行 1 分钟、总时长 6 分 40 秒为例：前两轮用掉 6 分钟，剩下 40 秒不足以完成第三轮跑步，因此第三轮只排 40 秒跑步并标记为不完整；跑步合计 4 分 40 秒，步行合计 2 分钟。

两种模式都不做“凑整轮”的额外处理。总时长模式下，计划严格等于你输入的总时长；循环数模式下，计划严格等于循环数乘以单轮时长。

## 输入与边界

- 跑步时长必须为大于零的整数秒。
- 步行时长可以为 0，但必须是非负整数秒。
- 循环数必须是 1 到 1000 之间的整数。
- 总时长必须是大于零的整数秒，且不超过 7 天（604,800 秒）；循环模式的计划总时长同样不能超过 7 天。
- 计划最多生成 3000 个分段；过短的单段配上很长的总时长会触发这一限制。

这些边界只保证算术可执行，不代表计划适合你的体能、伤病状况或训练阶段。工具不会判断跑走比例是否合理，也不会替你增减训练量。

## 怎样使用结果

逐段表适合用于间歇走跑、恢复期重返跑步，或把一段较长的活动拆成可管理的节奏。它也可以作为手动输入运动手表的草稿。计划里的时间都是**时钟时间**，不包含热身、冷身、补给或交通时间；如果需要把这些加进去，请自行在计划外安排。

如果你只想换算配速、距离和时间，使用[配速计算器](/tools/pace/)；如果要为一段目标时间安排每公里或每英里的分段，使用[分段配速表](/tools/splits/)。NHS 的 Couch to 5K 初学者计划是第一周以 1 分钟跑步配合 1 分 30 秒步行的公开例子；本工具引用它说明跑走交替的常见结构，不复制其训练处方，也不声称任何比例适合所有人。

## 验证算例

- 跑步 120 秒、步行 60 秒、3 轮：总时长 540 秒，共 6 段；跑步合计 360 秒，步行合计 180 秒，末段完整。
- 跑步 120 秒、步行 60 秒、总时长 400 秒：两轮完整循环用掉 360 秒，最后 40 秒为不完整跑步段；跑步合计 280 秒，步行合计 120 秒。
- 跑步 90 秒、步行 0 秒、2 轮：总时长 180 秒，只有两段跑步，没有零长度步行段。

这些数值由独立算术核对，不依赖页面脚本自身的输出。

## 隐私与数据

所有计算在浏览器本地完成，不上传到应用数据库，也不需要账户。为了刷新后恢复和分享，输入会写入当前网址的查询参数；打开或刷新页面时该网址会随请求发送到静态托管方，也会留在浏览器历史中。文件内容不会写入网址。公共设备上使用后请清除地址栏参数。

## 来源与适用范围

跑走交替的结构参考 NHS 的 Couch to 5K 初学者计划页面。该来源用于说明“短跑与步行交替”这一公开做法，不构成对具体人群的训练建议。本文与工具核验日期为 2026-10-27。身体不适、受伤或存在心血管风险时，请咨询合格的医疗或运动专业人员。

translations.title: Run-walk planner: cycles or total duration
translations.summary: Plan run-walk intervals. Enter a run and walk duration, then lay out the intervals by number of cycles or by total time, marking any truncated final segment. Time arithmetic only; no distance, pace or fitness estimate.
translations.body:
## What this tool answers

The run-walk planner turns "how long do I run, how long do I walk, and how many rounds" into a segment-by-segment schedule you can follow. It has two input modes:

- **Cycles mode**: given a run duration, a walk duration and a number of cycles, it lists the run and walk segments for every cycle. The walk in the final cycle is part of the plan and is not dropped.
- **Duration mode**: given a run duration, a walk duration and a total time, it starts at cycle one and keeps adding segments until the total is used up. If the total lands in the middle of a segment, that final segment is cut at the boundary and marked incomplete.

The output includes the requested duration, scheduled duration, number of full cycles, every segment, total running time, total walking time and whether the plan was truncated. It does not infer how far you travelled and does not estimate calories.

## How the two modes work

**Cycles mode**: each cycle is exactly "run then walk". For example, running 2 minutes and walking 1 minute for 3 cycles gives a total of 3 × (2 + 1) = 9 minutes, with 6 minutes of running and 3 minutes of walking across 6 segments. If the walk duration is zero, no empty walk rows are produced and the plan contains only runs.

**Duration mode**: the tool repeats run and walk until the requested total is reached. Take a 2-minute run, 1-minute walk and a total of 6 minutes 40 seconds. The first two full cycles use 6 minutes, leaving 40 seconds, which is not enough for the third run; the plan ends with a 40-second partial run. Running totals 4 minutes 40 seconds and walking totals 2 minutes.

Neither mode rounds up to a tidy number of cycles. Duration mode ends exactly at the entered total; cycles mode ends exactly at cycles multiplied by the cycle length.

## Inputs and limits

- The run duration must be a positive whole number of seconds.
- The walk duration may be zero but must be a non-negative whole number of seconds.
- The number of cycles must be a whole number from 1 to 1000.
- The total duration must be a positive whole number of seconds and no more than 7 days (604,800 seconds).
- A plan generates at most 3,000 segments; a very short segment combined with a very long total will hit this limit. The scheduled total in cycles mode is also limited to 7 days.

These limits only keep the arithmetic bounded. They do not mean the plan suits your fitness, injury history or training stage. The tool does not judge whether a run-walk ratio is reasonable and does not add or remove training load.

## Using the result

A segment list is useful for run-walk intervals, returning to running after a break, or breaking a longer outing into manageable pieces. It can also serve as a draft for manual watch entry. All times are **clock time** and exclude warm-up, cool-down, aid stops and travel; arrange those outside the plan if you need them.

For pace, distance and time conversion, use the [pace calculator](/en/tools/pace/). To plan per-kilometre or per-mile splits for a target time, use the [split table](/en/tools/splits/). The NHS Couch to 5K beginner plan is a public example whose first week uses 1-minute runs with 1-minute-30-second walks; this tool cites it to show a common run-walk structure, not to copy its training prescription or to claim that any ratio suits everyone.

## Verification cases

- Run 120 seconds, walk 60 seconds, 3 cycles: 540 seconds across 6 segments; running totals 360 seconds, walking totals 180 seconds, and the final segment is complete.
- Run 120 seconds, walk 60 seconds, total 400 seconds: two full cycles use 360 seconds, leaving a 40-second partial run; running totals 280 seconds and walking totals 120 seconds.
- Run 90 seconds, walk 0 seconds, 2 cycles: 180 seconds in two run segments with no zero-length walk rows.

These values were checked by independent arithmetic, not by the page script itself.

## Privacy and data

All calculations happen locally in your browser; inputs are not sent to an application database and no account is required. To restore inputs after a refresh and to support sharing, values are written into the page URL query string. Opening or refreshing that URL sends it to the static host and leaves it in browser history. File contents are never written into the URL. Clear the address-bar parameters after using a shared device.

## Sources and scope

The run-walk structure follows the NHS Couch to 5K beginner plan page. That source documents a public example of alternating short runs and walks; it is not a training recommendation for a particular person. This article and tool were checked on 2026-10-27. If you feel unwell, are injured or have cardiovascular risk factors, consult a qualified medical or sports professional.

translations.title: 跑鞋里程记录：本地管理训练鞋使用量
translations.summary: 记录每双跑鞋的初始里程、每次跑步距离和自定义提醒里程。工具只汇总本地数据，不声称统一更换里程，也不上传记录。
translations.body:
## 记录什么

为每双鞋取一个名字，填写购买时已有的里程（没有就填 0）和你希望收到提醒的里程。之后每次跑完记录日期、鞋和距离；工具会汇总累计里程、记录次数、距离提醒还有多少，以及提醒进度。

提醒里程由你设定，不是厂商建议，也不是“超过就必须扔”的寿命线。不同泡棉、外底、体重、路面和训练方式都会影响磨损。

## 提醒里程不是寿命

跑鞋没有适用于所有人的统一更换里程。外底磨穿、泡棉明显塌陷、鞋面破损、左右不对称磨损，或鞋子开始引起新的疼痛，比一个数字更值得关注。把提醒当作“检查一下”的信号，而不是自动更换指令。

轮换多双鞋可以分散磨损，但“必须轮换”或“只能穿一双”都没有适合所有人的证据。记录几双鞋的使用量，能帮助你看见哪双鞋在什么路面和距离下更舒服。

## 本地数据与隐私

记录保存在当前浏览器的 localStorage 中，不会上传到服务器，也不需要账户。清除浏览器数据、换设备或无痕窗口会让记录消失；如果记录重要，请自己导出或备份。

工具不读取你的位置、轨迹或健康数据，只保存鞋名、日期和距离。不要在鞋名中写入住址、姓名或其他敏感信息。

## 什么时候检查或更换

每次长距离后检查外底、鞋头和鞋面；如果抓地明显下降、泡棉失去弹性、鞋面破损或持续不适，考虑更换。新鞋仍需逐渐适应，不要在比赛日第一次穿。

如果疼痛持续、肿胀、麻木或步态改变，先停止相关训练并寻求医疗或运动专业人士评估；换鞋不一定能解决负荷或技术问题。

## 适用边界

本工具不推荐品牌或型号，不判断鞋是否“报废”，也不诊断足部或下肢疼痛。提醒里程只是用户设置的个人管理值。

## 来源与适用范围

鞋类舒适度与伤病关联参考次要分析；跑鞋、疼痛与就医提示参考 NHS；碳板与先进鞋款的证据边界参考系统综述。工具只负责本地汇总，不对鞋的寿命或安全性作保证。

translations.title: Shoe mileage log: manage training-shoe use locally
translations.summary: Record each shoe's starting mileage, run distances and a user-set reminder. The tool only totals local data; it does not claim a universal replacement mileage and never uploads the log.
translations.body:
## What to record

Give each pair a name, enter any distance already on it (use 0 if new) and the mileage at which you want a reminder. After each run, record the date, shoe and distance. The tool totals mileage, run count, distance remaining to the reminder and reminder progress.

The reminder is your own setting, not a manufacturer recommendation or a “replace at this number” lifespan. Foam, outsole, body weight, surface and training style all affect wear.

## A reminder is not a lifespan

There is no universal replacement mileage for running shoes. Worn-through outsole, collapsed foam, a torn upper, markedly asymmetric wear or new pain are more useful signals than a single number. Treat the reminder as a prompt to inspect the shoe, not an automatic replacement order.

Rotating several pairs may spread wear, but neither “always rotate” nor “always use one pair” is supported for everyone. Logging a few pairs helps you see which shoe feels better on which surface and distance.

## Local data and privacy

Records are stored in this browser's localStorage. They are not uploaded to a server and no account is required. Clearing browser data, changing devices or using a private window can remove the log; back it up yourself if it matters.

The tool does not read location, track files or health data. It stores only shoe names, dates and distances. Do not put addresses, names or other sensitive information in a shoe name.

## When to inspect or replace

Check the outsole, toe box and upper after long runs. Consider replacement when grip falls clearly, foam loses resilience, the upper tears or the shoe keeps causing discomfort. New shoes still need gradual adaptation; do not wear them for the first time on race day.

If pain persists, or you notice swelling, numbness or a change in gait, stop the relevant training and seek medical or sports-professional assessment; a new shoe may not fix load or technique issues.

## Tool limits

This tool does not recommend brands or models, decide whether a shoe is “dead” or diagnose foot or lower-limb pain. The reminder is a personal management value.

## Sources and scope

Shoe comfort and injury associations follow a secondary analysis; shoe, pain and help-seeking advice follows the NHS; carbon-plate and advanced-footwear evidence follows a systematic review. The tool only totals local records and does not guarantee shoe lifespan or safety.

translations.title: 分段配速表：把目标成绩拆成每一段
translations.summary: 输入总距离、总时间和分段距离，选择匀速或负分段策略，生成可打印的分段表。最后一段可以不满一个单位，所有整数秒严格加总为总时间。
translations.body:
## 用途

分段配速表把一次目标成绩拆成相同距离的分段，适合赛前写配速手环、打印贴在补给包上，或赛后对照实际分段。它提供两种明确的算术策略：**匀速**和**负分段**。两者都是计划工具，不是对比赛过程的预测。

例如：10 公里目标 50 分钟，按 1 公里匀速分段，每一段 5 分钟，累计 5、10、15……50 分钟。5 公里按 2 公里分段时，前两段各 10 分钟，最后 1 公里 5 分钟。

## 两种策略

**匀速**：每一米都使用同一个配速，即总时间 ÷ 总距离。

**负分段**：前半程按距离较慢，后半程较快。差值 `delta` 默认 0.02，允许 0 到 0.10。前半程使用总时间的 `(1 + delta) ÷ 2`，后半程使用 `(1 − delta) ÷ 2`。以 10 公里 3000 秒、delta = 0.02 为例，前半程 5 公里用 1530 秒（306 秒/公里），后半程 5 公里用 1470 秒（294 秒/公里）。

跨越中点的分段会按两段实际里程分别积分，不会把整段错误地套用同一种配速。

## 算法

1. 分段数 = 总距离 ÷ 分段距离，向上取整。
2. 第 i 段的起止距离为 `[(i−1) × 分段距离, min(i × 分段距离, 总距离)]`。
3. 匀速策略下，精确时间 = 该段米数 × 总秒数 ÷ 总米数。
4. 负分段策略下，按该段落在前半程、后半程或跨越中点的部分，分别乘以对应配速后相加。
5. 对每段精确时间取下整，再用**最大余数法**分配剩余整数秒：小数部分最大的分段各加 1 秒，余数相同时优先靠前的分段。
6. 最后一段仍可不满一个分段单位，但所有段时间相加严格等于总时间，且不出现负分段。

最大余数法可能让某一段与精确值相差一秒，但总时间不会漂移。表格中的累计时间由整数分段直接累加，因此不会出现末段为负或总计对不上的情况。

## 输入与边界

- 总距离、总时间、分段距离都必须大于零；总时间按整数秒输入。
- `delta` 只对负分段生效，范围为 0 到 0.10；设为 0 时与匀速结果相同。
- 分段距离大于总距离时，只生成一段，时间等于总时间。
- 距离单位可选公里或英里；表内单位与输入一致，英里按 1,609.344 米换算。
- 工具不根据坡度、补给或天气调整配速。这些属于训练与比赛决策，不应由一个算术表替你决定。

## 怎样使用

把表当作**目标的上界或参考**。比赛起跑、补给、坡度和天气会让实际分段不同；如果前半程明显快于表，后半程可能付出代价。负分段表描述的是你主动选择的配速分布，不是保证后半程一定更快。

需要先换算平均配速，可使用[配速计算器](/tools/pace/)。理解马拉松标准距离，可阅读[马拉松为什么是 42.195 公里](https://learn.paobu.org/articles/marathon-distance/)。

## 验证算例

- 10 公里、3000 秒、1 公里匀速：10 段，每段 300 秒，累计从 300 到 3000 秒。
- 5 公里、1500 秒、2 公里匀速：3 段，距离 2、2、1 公里，时间 600、600、300 秒，总计 1500 秒。
- 5 英里、2400 秒、1 英里匀速：5 段，每段 480 秒，总计 2400 秒。
- 10 公里、3000 秒、4 公里负分段、delta = 0.02：时间为 1224、1188、588 秒，总计 3000 秒；第二段跨过中点。
- 10 公里、3000 秒、5 公里负分段、delta = 0.02：前半程 1530 秒，后半程 1470 秒。

所有算例均由独立算术核对。

## 隐私与数据

所有计算在浏览器本地完成，不上传到应用数据库，也不需要账户。为了刷新后恢复和分享，输入会写入当前网址的查询参数；打开或刷新页面时该网址会随请求发送到静态托管方，也会留在浏览器历史中。文件内容不会写入网址。公共设备上使用后请清除地址栏参数。

## 来源与适用范围

距离单位与马拉松标准值依据 World Athletics 的说明。本文与工具核验日期为 2026-10-27。分段表不构成完赛承诺。

translations.title: Split table: break a target time into segments
translations.summary: Enter total distance, total time and split distance, then choose an even or negative-split strategy to build a printable table. The final segment may be short, and all whole seconds add up exactly to the total.
translations.body:
## What it is for

A split table breaks a target performance into equal-distance segments. It is useful for writing a pace band before a race, printing a note for an aid-station bag, or comparing actual splits afterwards. It offers two explicit arithmetic strategies: **even** and **negative split**. Both are planning tools, not predictions of how a race will unfold.

For example: 10 km in 50 minutes with 1 km even splits gives 5 minutes per segment and cumulative times of 5, 10, 15 … 50 minutes. For 5 km with 2 km splits, the first two segments take 10 minutes each and the final 1 km takes 5 minutes.

## The two strategies

**Even**: every metre uses the same pace, total time ÷ total distance.

**Negative split**: the first half of the distance is slower and the second half is faster. The difference `delta` defaults to 0.02 and is limited to 0 to 0.10. The first half uses `(1 + delta) ÷ 2` of total time and the second half uses `(1 − delta) ÷ 2`. For 10 km in 3000 seconds with delta = 0.02, the first 5 km take 1530 seconds (306 s/km) and the second 5 km take 1470 seconds (294 s/km).

A segment that crosses the halfway point is integrated over its actual metres in each half; the whole segment is never given a single pace by mistake.

## The algorithm

1. Split count = total distance ÷ split distance, rounded up.
2. Segment i covers `[(i−1) × split distance, min(i × split distance, total distance)]`.
3. Under the even strategy, exact time = segment metres × total seconds ÷ total metres.
4. Under the negative strategy, each part before or after the halfway distance is multiplied by its own pace, then the parts are added.
5. Take the floor of every exact time, then distribute the remaining whole seconds by **largest remainder**: the segments with the largest fractional parts receive one extra second each, with ties going to the earlier segment.
6. The final segment may still be shorter than a full unit, but every segment time adds up exactly to the total and no segment is negative.

Largest-remainder allocation can put a segment one second away from its exact value, but the total does not drift. Cumulative times are built from the allocated whole seconds, so the last segment cannot turn negative and the total cannot disagree with the input.

## Inputs and limits

- Total distance, total time and split distance must all be greater than zero; total time is entered as whole seconds.
- `delta` applies only to the negative strategy and must be between 0 and 0.10; setting it to 0 produces the same table as the even strategy.
- If the split distance is greater than the total distance, the table has one segment equal to the total time.
- Distance units can be kilometres or miles; the table uses the unit you entered, with one mile equal to 1,609.344 metres.
- The tool does not adjust for hills, aid stations or weather. Those are training and racing decisions, not arithmetic the table should make for you.

## How to use it

Treat the table as a **reference or ceiling**, not a command. Start corrals, aid stations, hills and weather will move actual splits. If the first half is clearly faster than the table, the second half may pay for it. A negative-split table describes a deliberate pace distribution; it does not guarantee that the second half will feel easier.

To convert an average pace first, use the [pace calculator](/en/tools/pace/). To understand the standard marathon distance, read [why the marathon is 42.195 km](https://learn.paobu.org/en/articles/marathon-distance/).

## Verification cases

- 10 km, 3000 seconds, 1 km even splits: 10 segments of 300 seconds, cumulative from 300 to 3000 seconds.
- 5 km, 1500 seconds, 2 km even splits: 3 segments of 2, 2 and 1 km, taking 600, 600 and 300 seconds, totalling 1500 seconds.
- 5 miles, 2400 seconds, 1 mile even splits: 5 segments of 480 seconds, totalling 2400 seconds.
- 10 km, 3000 seconds, 4 km negative splits, delta = 0.02: 1224, 1188 and 588 seconds, totalling 3000 seconds; the second segment crosses halfway.
- 10 km, 3000 seconds, 5 km negative splits, delta = 0.02: 1530 seconds for the first half and 1470 seconds for the second half.

All cases were checked by independent arithmetic.

## Privacy and data

All calculations happen locally in your browser; inputs are not sent to an application database and no account is required. To restore inputs after a refresh and to support sharing, values are written into the page URL query string. Opening or refreshing that URL sends it to the static host and leaves it in browser history. File contents are never written into the URL. Clear the address-bar parameters after using a shared device.

## Sources and scope

Distance units and the standard marathon value follow World Athletics' description. This article and tool were checked on 2026-10-27. A split table is not a finish-time promise.

translations.title: 轨迹格式转换：GPX 与 GeoJSON 线路互转
translations.summary: 在浏览器本地把 GPX 或 GeoJSON 线路转换为另一种格式，保留坐标顺序与已有高程，并主动剥离时间、设备、姓名和原始 metadata。
translations.body:
## 这个工具做什么

轨迹格式转换读取一条线路，按你选择的输出格式重新写出文件，并提供下载。它适合把手表或应用导出的 GPX 变成 GeoJSON，或把 GeoJSON 线路变成 GPX 交给其他工具，而不把原始文件里的个人信息一起带过去。

转换输出包括线路几何、坐标顺序、每个线段的分段关系，以及点上有可靠高程时的 `<ele>` 或第三个坐标值。工具不会写入时间戳、设备名称、人名、文件名或其他原始 metadata。它也不会把缺失的高程补成 0。

## 接受哪些输入

- **GPX**：优先读取 `trk` 下的 `trkseg`；如果没有 `trkseg`，再读取路线 `rte`。每个 `trkseg` 或 `rte` 作为独立线段处理，不把不同线段的端点连接起来。
- **GeoJSON**：接受 `LineString`、`MultiLineString`，以及只包含这些类型的 `FeatureCollection` 或 `Feature`。坐标顺序固定为经度、纬度，第三位可选高程。

点集、多边形或其他非线路几何类型会被拒绝并报错，而不是被悄悄转换成一条假线路。文件上限为 20 MB、200,000 个坐标点；仅支持本地读取，不上传服务器。

## 输出与隐私

输出是重新序列化的文件，因此即使输出格式与输入相同，字节内容也可能与原始文件不同，例如缩进、数字写法或元素顺序会变化。需要保留原始文件时，请自行保留；工具不会修改或覆盖它。

下载文件由浏览器在本地生成。文件内容不会上传、不会写入服务器日志，也不会在刷新后保留。公共设备上处理含家庭住址的轨迹时，请先考虑是否适合打开。

## 验证算例

一条包含三个点的 GeoJSON 线路：`[0, 0, 10]`、`[0.001, 0]`、`[0.002, 0, 15]`。转换后仍应只有一个线段、三个坐标点，其中两个点带高程（10 与 15），中间点没有高程。坐标顺序与数值不得改变，缺失高程不能用 `null` 或 0 冒充。该算例由独立往返检查核对，不依赖页面脚本的显示结果。

## 不能回答的问题

转换工具不判断线路是否为官方赛道、是否获得通行许可、是否适合比赛，也不认证距离。它只改变文件格式。若要读取距离、点数与起终点，使用[轨迹查看](/tools/track-view/)；若要减少点数，使用[轨迹简化](/tools/track-simplify/)并在输出中核对点数与距离变化。

## 来源与适用范围

文件结构依据 GPX 1.1 规范与 RFC 7946 GeoJSON 规范。本文与工具核验日期为 2026-10-27。

translations.title: Track conversion: GPX and GeoJSON lines
translations.summary: Convert a GPX or GeoJSON line to the other format in your browser, preserving coordinate order and available elevation while stripping times, devices, names and original metadata.
translations.body:
## What this tool does

The track converter reads a line and writes it again in the format you choose, then offers the result as a download. It is useful for turning a watch or app GPX export into GeoJSON, or a GeoJSON line into GPX for another tool, without carrying the original file's personal information across.

The output contains the line geometry, the coordinate order, the separation between segments and, where a point has reliable elevation, an `<ele>` element or a third coordinate value. The tool does not write timestamps, device names, person names, file names or other original metadata. It also does not replace missing elevation with zero.

## Accepted input

- **GPX**: reads `trkseg` elements under `trk`; if there is no `trkseg`, it reads route `rte` elements instead. Every `trkseg` or `rte` becomes an independent segment; endpoints of different segments are not joined.
- **GeoJSON**: accepts `LineString`, `MultiLineString`, and `FeatureCollection` or `Feature` wrappers containing only those types. Coordinates are longitude, latitude, with an optional third elevation value.

Point sets, polygons and other non-line geometry types are rejected with an error rather than silently turned into a fake line. Files are limited to 20 MB and 200,000 points and are read locally; nothing is uploaded.

## Output and privacy

The output is re-serialized, so even when the output format matches the input the bytes may differ from the original: indentation, number formatting or element order can change. Keep your original file if you need it; the tool never modifies or overwrites it.

The download is generated locally by the browser. Its content is not uploaded, written to server logs or retained after a refresh. On a shared device, think twice before opening a track that reveals a home address.

## Verification case

A GeoJSON line with three points: `[0, 0, 10]`, `[0.001, 0]`, `[0.002, 0, 15]`. After conversion it must still have one segment and three positions, two of which carry elevation (10 and 15) while the middle point has none. Coordinate order and values must not change; missing elevation must not be replaced by `null` or zero. This case was checked by an independent round trip, not by the page's display output.

## What it cannot answer

The converter does not decide whether a line is an official course, whether access is permitted or whether it is suitable for a race, and it does not certify distance. It only changes the file format. To read distance, point count and endpoints, use the [track viewer](/en/tools/track-view/). To reduce the number of points, use [track simplification](/en/tools/track-simplify/) and check the reported points and distance change.

## Sources and scope

The file structure follows the GPX 1.1 specification and RFC 7946 for GeoJSON. This article and tool were checked on 2026-10-27.

translations.title: 轨迹简化：按投影容差减少点数并对照距离
translations.summary: 对每个线段独立做本地米制投影与迭代 RDP 简化，保留端点与断段关系，并展示简化前后的点数与 WGS84 距离变化。原始文件不被修改。
translations.body:
## 这个工具做什么

轨迹简化读取 GPX 或 GeoJSON 线路，在每个线段内部按给定容差去除对形状影响较小的点，生成一个新的简化文件供下载，同时显示简化前后的点数、WGS84 测地距离和逐段对照。它不会修改或覆盖你选择的原始文件。

简化是**有损**的：被删除的点及其高程不会再出现在输出中；保留下来的点使用原始坐标与原始高程，不做平滑、不重新采样，也不会把断开的线段连接起来。

## 方法

1. 对每个线段分别计算平均纬度，并在该纬度附近做本地等距投影，把经度、纬度换算成米。
2. 在这个投影平面上运行迭代版 Ramer–Douglas–Peucker（RDP）算法：先保留首尾点，再反复找出离当前弦最远的点；若距离超过容差就保留它，并把线段在该点处继续拆分。
3. 按原始顺序输出保留点，再以 WGS84 椭球逆解重新计算简化前后的距离。

容差是**投影平面上的米数**，不是测地距离。由于投影是局部近似，远离投影中心时容差与实际地面距离会有细微差别；页面同时报告简化前后的 WGS84 距离，便于判断形状变化是否可接受。RDP 的容差只约束点到弦的偏差，不保证距离变化一定落在同一数值内。

## 容差与拒绝条件

容差必须为 1 到 100 米，页面初始值为 10 米。文件上限为 20 MB、200,000 个坐标点。首版对以下线段**拒绝简化**，并指出具体段号：

- 单段投影包围盒对角线超过 500 公里。
- 经度跨度超过 180 度，视为可能跨越日界线。
- 任一点纬度超过 85 度。

这些限制只针对简化。同一文件仍可用[轨迹查看](/tools/track-view/)读取统计，或用[轨迹转换](/tools/track-convert/)改格式。简化输出保持输入格式；若输入是 GPX，输出仍是 GPX，若输入是 GeoJSON，输出仍是 GeoJSON。

## 验证算例

赤道附近三点：`[0, 0]`、`[0.001, 0.00005]`、`[0.002, 0]`，容差 10 米。中间点相对首尾弦的纬度偏移约 0.00005 度，即约 5.56 米，小于 10 米，因此被移除；输出保留首尾两点。若容差改为 1 米，中间点会被保留。该算例由独立算术核对，不依赖页面脚本自身的输出。

## 隐私与限制

文件只在浏览器内读取和计算，不上传服务器，也不会在刷新后保留。工具不判断轨迹是否为官方赛道、是否安全或是否适合比赛，简化后的距离也不是赛事丈量。若需要分享文件，建议先检查起点附近是否包含家庭住址等敏感位置。

## 来源与适用范围

RDP 算法参考 Ramer（1972）与 Douglas–Peucker（1973）的论文记录；坐标与测地距离口径遵循 WGS84 与 core 的 GeographicLib 实现。本文与工具核验日期为 2026-10-27。

translations.title: Track simplification: projected tolerance, point and distance comparison
translations.summary: Simplify each segment independently with a local metric projection and iterative RDP, keeping endpoints and segment breaks while reporting the change in points and WGS84 distance. The original file is never modified.
translations.body:
## What this tool does

The simplifier reads a GPX or GeoJSON line, removes points that contribute little to its shape within a chosen tolerance, and produces a new simplified file for download. It reports the number of points before and after, the WGS84 geodesic distance before and after, and a per-segment comparison. It does not modify or overwrite the original file.

Simplification is **lossy**: removed points and their elevation values do not appear in the output; retained points keep their original coordinates and elevation. The tool does not smooth or resample the line and does not join separate segments.

## Method

1. For each segment, compute its mean latitude and project longitude and latitude to local metres around that latitude.
2. Run an iterative Ramer–Douglas–Peucker (RDP) pass in the projected plane: keep the first and last points, repeatedly find the point farthest from the current chord, keep it when the distance exceeds the tolerance, and continue on both sides.
3. Output the retained points in their original order and recompute the distance before and after using WGS84 geodesic inverse distances.

The tolerance is a number of **projected metres**, not a geodesic distance. Because the projection is a local approximation, the tolerance and ground distance can differ slightly away from the projection centre; the page reports the WGS84 distance change separately so you can judge whether the shape change is acceptable. RDP constrains the deviation of points from a chord; it does not guarantee that the total distance changes by the same amount.

## Tolerance and refusal conditions

The tolerance is required, must be between 1 and 100 metres, and the page starts at 10 metres. Files are limited to 20 MB and 200,000 coordinate points. This version **refuses to simplify** a segment, and names the segment, when:

- its projected bounding-box diagonal exceeds 500 km;
- its longitude span exceeds 180 degrees, which may indicate an antimeridian crossing;
- any point lies beyond 85 degrees latitude.

These limits apply only to simplification. The same file can still be read with the [track viewer](/en/tools/track-view/) or converted with the [track converter](/en/tools/track-convert/). The output keeps the input format: GPX stays GPX and GeoJSON stays GeoJSON.

## Verification case

Three points near the equator: `[0, 0]`, `[0.001, 0.00005]`, `[0.002, 0]`, with a tolerance of 10 metres. The middle point deviates from the chord by about 0.00005 degrees of latitude, roughly 5.56 metres, which is below 10 metres, so it is removed and the endpoints remain. At a 1-metre tolerance the middle point is kept. This case was checked by independent arithmetic, not by the page script itself.

## Privacy and limits

The file is read and processed only in your browser. It is not uploaded and is not retained after a refresh. The tool does not decide whether a track is an official course, safe or suitable for a race, and the simplified distance is not a certified measurement. Before sharing a file, check whether it reveals sensitive locations such as a home address.

## Sources and scope

The RDP method follows Ramer (1972) and Douglas–Peucker (1973); coordinate and distance handling follow WGS84 and the GeographicLib implementation used by core. This article and tool were checked on 2026-10-27.
